 Petrol price cut by Rs5.45 per litre, diesel rate increased by Rs3.68 
 Web Desk 11:30 PM | November 03, 2026 Business Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Twitter The federal government has lowered the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre but raised the rate of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.68 for the latest pricing period, according to an official notification issued on Tuesday.
 Under the revised rates, petrol will now cost Rs369.06 per litre, compared with the previous Rs374.51. The price of high-speed diesel has been increased from Rs391.52 to Rs395.20 per litre.
 Pakistan secures 11 China education deals for youth skills 
 The new prices will come into force at midnight on November 4 and remain effective until the next review.
 The adjustment offers some relief to users of petrol-powered vehicles, including motorcycles and cars, while increasing fuel expenses for diesel consumers. The higher diesel rate may also add to operating costs for transport and logistics businesses, as HSD is commonly used by buses, trucks, heavy vehicles and agricultural machinery. Any rise in transportation expenses could put further pressure on the prices of essential goods.
 The revision comes amid government efforts to address the financial difficulties faced by consumers. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said earlier on Tuesday that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had instructed relevant authorities to prepare a winter gas supply plan and take measures to protect vulnerable segments of society.

 Speaking at a press conference, Tarar said the government was mindful of the financial challenges facing ordinary citizens. He added that Rs15 billion in refinery profits had been transferred to the public and that profiteering by certain operators in the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sector had been curbed.
 Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said Pakistan had been facing economic pressures linked to the conflict that began on February 28. He noted that international oil prices had declined and expressed hope that the global market trend would lead to further relief for consumers.
